issues.legal_issue: A compulsory acquisition law must provide compensation through an amount or valuation principles that are relevant and non-arbitrary in relation to the property’s value at or about the time of acquisition.
material_facts: The law acquired an undertaking and calculated compensation by valuing its assets and subtracting its liabilities.
Unused machinery in good condition was valued at its historical purchase cost, while other machinery was valued at its tax written-down value.
The historical-cost method did not account for later increases in machinery prices, and tax depreciation did not necessarily reflect machinery’s actual value.
Machinery was a major part of the undertaking.
issues.conclusion: The valuation principles for machinery were irrelevant to its value at acquisition and did not provide compensation within the constitutional meaning; the acquisition law was unconstitutional.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 31(2) of the Constitution, a law compulsorily acquiring property must provide compensation and either fix its amount or specify principles and a manner for determining it. The principles must be relevant and non-arbitrary and must provide a just equivalent by reference to value at or about acquisition; once they meet that test, the adequacy of the resulting compensation is beyond judicial scrutiny. The Court applied State of West Bengal v. Mrs. Bela Banerjee, State of Madras v. D. Namasivaya Mudaliar, Vajravelu v. Special Deputy Collector, and Jeejeebhoy v. Assistant Collector.

predicates.compulsory_acquisition_law: A law provides for the compulsory acquisition of property.
predicates.unused_equipment_valued_at_historical_co: The law values unused equipment in good condition by the cost incurred to acquire it, without regard to its value at acquisition.
predicates.used_equipment_valued_by_tax_write_down: The law values used equipment by a tax write-down measure rather than its actual value at acquisition.
predicates.valuation_basis_unrelated_to_value_at_ac: The valuation methods do not provide a relevant measure of the property’s value at or about the time it is acquired.
predicates.acquisition_law_unconstitutional: The acquisition law is unconstitutional for failing to provide constitutionally valid compensation.

issues.definition: When an acquisition law uses both historical cost for unused equipment and tax write-down value for used equipment, and those measures are unrelated to value at acquisition, the law is unconstitutional.

issues.legal_issue: Invalid valuation principles for a major asset cannot be severed from the compensation scheme when the undertaking is acquired as a unit and no offsetting compensation is shown.
material_facts: The entire undertaking was acquired as a unit, and the law treated compensation as a single amount for the undertaking as a whole.
The invalid valuation principles applied to machinery, which was a major part of the undertaking.
It was not shown that higher compensation for other assets would offset the deficiency in the machinery valuation.
issues.conclusion: The invalid machinery valuation provisions were not severable from the compensation scheme, and their invalidity affected the total compensation for the undertaking.
issues.legal_principle: Because compensation was determined for the undertaking as a whole by adding valuations of its parts, invalid principles governing a major part affected the total compensation. The Court held that the valuation clauses were not severable in this context; the conclusion formed part of its application of Article 31(2) and its reasoning in Vajravelu v. Special Deputy Collector and Jeejeebhoy v. Assistant Collector.

rule.if: undertaking_acquired_as_unit and invalid_valuation_applies_to_major_asset and not demonstrated_offsetting_compensation

predicates.undertaking_acquired_as_unit: The property acquired is an undertaking treated as one unit for compensation.
predicates.invalid_valuation_applies_to_major_asset: An invalid valuation method applies to an asset that forms a major part of the undertaking.
predicates.demonstrated_offsetting_compensation: It is shown that higher valuation of other parts offsets the deficiency caused by the invalid valuation method.
predicates.compensation_scheme_not_severable: The invalid valuation provisions cannot be separated from the compensation scheme for the undertaking.

issues.definition: When an undertaking is acquired as a unit, an invalid valuation method applies to a major asset, and no offsetting compensation is demonstrated, the compensation scheme is not severable.
